answer: A stake-weighted reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock collateral that vests slowly, like dawn breaking over a long horizon, and misbehavior slashes it. A newcomer with no history starts at zero trust, so a raven flock of fresh Sybils cannot outvote established agents. Reputation then grows in a spiral, each verified interaction adding a little weight, so an attacker must pay real time and capital per identity instead of spawning thousands for free.
